# /crav1-code-into-specs

[All skills](../skills.md) · Walkthrough: [From a code change onto existing specs](../../from-code.md) · Playbook: [`SKILL.md`](../../../.cursor/skills/crav1/crav1-code-into-specs/SKILL.md)

## Purpose

Sort a code change that already landed (a commit, a range, or the branch diff) onto specs that already exist.

A code change that already landed, specs already exist → sort onto those specs (belongs, already described there, or fits none), then quote what the change does. No dump. Does not ask for a slug first. Does not create a slug. Does not watch the repo. Does not seed `docs/system/`. Fills a missing `glossary.md` only when that folder already exists. New glossary rows are appended. Existing rows are not rewritten. A meaning the source does not state is `to be researched`. That same pass adds what is new to the short description, the diagram, and how the parts connect. It does not rewrite what is already there. Does not plan, implement, or commit.

## Runs when

A landed change; specs already exist. Called by the user.

## Reads

In short: A commit, range, or branch diff, plus specs.

Reads a named commit, range, or branch diff, and existing spec folders.

## Writes

In short: Quotes of what belongs in matching specs, a missing `glossary.md` or new glossary rows when `docs/system/` exists, the picture update, `Synced at` (repo cell or slice line), and research stale marks after a yes; other listed edits only on apply.

Writes quotes of what belongs into the matching `spec.md` files, and the same glossary gap as match-dump. When the read is a whole repo, sets that repo's `Synced at` cell and touches only those repos. When the read is one slice, leaves that column alone and writes or updates `Synced at: <repo> <branch>@<short sha>, <date>` on that slice's `spec.md`. After a kept quote, compares it with `docs/research/*.md` and `## Research findings` on the specs it touches, including notes those findings link to, following `crav1-add-to-spec` `references/research-stale.md`. A clear contradiction or an answered open question is marked stale only after the user says yes. An unclear case is not marked. It may draft a revisit request for the note's owner. It does not send it.

## Does not

Leaves leftovers, application code, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, and other landscape files alone unless the user picks apply. Does not commit.

Limits and exceptions: creates no slug, seeds no `docs/system/`, and does not watch the repo. The research question is not the landscape apply question. A skill that writes `docs/research/` follows the clear section of that same file. That check does not ask the user.

- Runs by itself: Calls no skill.
